consensus_summary: Door/gate primarily symbolizes access/entrance to God, salvation, and eternal life, with Christ as the exclusive door/gate (John 10); alternatives include open opportunity for ministry, civic authority/power (gates of Hades), door of the heart, eschatological exclusion, and minority typological OT prefigurations (Passover posts, ark, etc.).
book_summary: The destination of the way — the entrance to the house of God, marked on the posts.
consensus_core_identification: Access/entrance to God and salvation, characteristically Christ himself as the exclusive door/gate.
book_core_identification: Entrance to the house of God (as destination of the way), marked on the posts.
boundary_disagreement: Book definitionally centers the house-of-God entrance that is marked on the posts and functions as destination of the way; consensus treats post-marking and house-of-God access as secondary/typological while admitting many other contextual extensions (opportunity, authority, heart, judgment) under a broader access category.
rationale: Minimum cores share the general referent of entrance/access into God's dwelling/presence/salvation (supported by shared John 10:9 citation). Book preserves that category but materially narrows and re-precisifies it by making 'house of God + marked posts + destination of the way' definitional, elevating what consensus lists only as minority typology (Ex 12 posts) or secondary motif while excluding or demoting other common consensus cases. This is boundary/precision disagreement, not replacement of the central access referent.
strongest_objection: Consensus primary is the direct Christological identification ('I am the door'); book's phrasing foregrounds architectural/ritual marking of the house entrance and may appear to treat Christology as secondary even while citing John 10:9.
